@graph.name: spdx-xsafety-sbom
@graph.description: SPDX 3.0.1 Design SBOM Generator v0.1.0

@graph.name: HAZ-001
@graph.description: If cam-service fails to detect a stream event temporal fault (event timeout / missed deadline), the critical application may continue operating with a latent malfunction without being reported to the Fault Manager.

extension.xSafety:severity: s2 (potential severe injuries if malfunction propagates)
extension.xSafety:exposure: e3 (medium probability of relevant operating situation)
extension.xSafety:controllability: c2 (difficult for driver/system to mitigate without detection)

@graph.comment: CAM is intended to detect temporal issues (events outside expected period) and raise a fault to a Fault Manager; missing this reduces fault coverage.

@graph.name: SG-001
@graph.description: CAM shall detect stream event temporal faults (including event timeouts) according to deployed configuration and report the fault to the platform Fault Manager within the configured monitoring timeout window.

@graph.name: HAZ-002
@graph.description: If cam-service fails to detect stream event logical faults (events arriving out of order), the critical application may produce incorrect outputs without being reported to the Fault Manager.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation states logical issues include events arriving out of order and cam-service can raise a stream event logic fault.

@graph.name: SG-002
@graph.description: CAM shall detect stream event logical faults (out-of-order events) and report the fault to the platform Fault Manager.

@graph.name: HAZ-003
@graph.description: If CAM fails to enforce stream state progression and timeouts (init→start and start→first event), monitoring may be inactive or misaligned, reducing fault detection coverage during operation.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes stream initialization/start/stop and state-control timeouts; cam-service reports stream state faults and state timeouts.

@graph.name: SG-003
@graph.description: CAM shall enforce stream state transitions and configured state-control timeouts and report violations to the Fault Manager.

@graph.name: HAZ-004
@graph.description: If CAM misinterprets timestamps (e.g., unsynchronized clocks) or does not apply a reasonable tolerance, it may raise spurious faults leading to unnecessary Fault Manager actions (degraded mode/reset), potentially impacting vehicle operation.

extension.xSafety:severity: s2 (potential hazardous behavior if unnecessary safe reaction occurs at inopportune time)
extension.xSafety:exposure: e2 (lower probability with time sync, but possible)

@graph.comment: CAM protocol requires synchronized clocks between cam-service, cam-tool and critical applications; cam-service implements a clock tolerance when checking message timestamps.

@graph.name: SG-004
@graph.description: CAM shall apply a timestamp sanity check (including an allowed tolerance) to detect implausible message timestamps and prevent unsafe monitoring behavior due to timebase anomalies.

@graph.name: HAZ-005
@graph.description: If CAM uses invalid or unintended deployment configuration (CSD), monitoring timeouts/order expectations may be wrong, leading to missed detections or spurious faults.
@graph.comment: CAM uses CSC converted to CSD and cam-service matches streams by UUID to load deployment data; deployment over network is documented as a convenience that should not be enabled in production.

@graph.name: SG-005
@graph.description: CAM shall only monitor streams against validated deployment data selected by stream UUID, and deployment-over-network shall be restricted to development lifecycle or otherwise controlled by platform policy.

@graph.name: TSR-001
@graph.description: cam-service shall monitor each configured event in a stream using the deployed per-event timeout values and shall raise a stream event temporal fault when an expected event deadline is missed.

@graph.name: TSR-002
@graph.description: cam-service shall detect out-of-order event arrival within each stream and shall raise a stream event logic fault when ordering is violated.

@graph.name: TSR-003
@graph.description: cam-service shall verify an event sequence identifier for each stream event message and shall raise a stream sequence fault when the received sequence does not match the expected sequence.

@graph.name: TSR-004
@graph.description: cam-service shall enforce stream state transitions and configured state-control timeouts (init→start, start→first-event) and shall raise a stream state fault or state timeout fault when violated.

@graph.name: TSR-005
@graph.description: On any detected monitoring violation (temporal, logical, sequence, state) and on unrecoverable internal service errors, cam-service shall report the fault to a platform Fault Manager driver interface.

@graph.name: TSR-006
@graph.description: cam-service shall apply a timestamp sanity check to received protocol messages (init/start/stop/event/deploy) and shall reject messages with timestamps implausibly in the future beyond a configured tolerance.

@graph.name: TSR-007
@graph.description: CAM shall bind monitoring to stream deployment data selected by stream UUID, and the CSC→CSD conversion and deployment process shall provide consistent, validated configuration data to cam-service.

@graph.name: TSR-008
@graph.description: libcam and cam-tool shall implement the Stream Message Protocol fields (including endianness and timestamps) to ensure cam-service can reliably monitor streams and process deployments.

@graph.name: SSR-001
@graph.description: cam-service shall, on receipt of a stream initialization message, allocate a stream handler on the connection, load stream deployment data by UUID, and reply with a status indicating success, out-of-resources, or no-configuration.
@graph.comment: CAM protocol and implementation allocate resources per stream and bind monitoring configuration to stream UUID.

@graph.name: SSR-002
@graph.description: cam-service shall enforce stream state progression such that stream events are only accepted when the stream is in the monitoring-in-progress state, and invalid state requests shall result in a reported stream state fault.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation identifies stream state faults; repo implementation reports state faults when messages do not match expected state.

@graph.name: SSR-003
@graph.description: cam-service shall implement and enforce configured state-control timeouts for init→start and start→first-event and shall report a stream state timeout fault when a timeout expires.
@graph.comment: CSC format defines state_control timeouts; cam-service implements state timers and reports state timeout faults.

@graph.name: SSR-004
@graph.description: cam-service shall validate message header protocol version and message sizing for received protocol messages and shall reject invalid messages without entering an unsafe monitoring state.
@graph.comment: Robust protocol handling prevents malformed messages from corrupting monitoring state.

@graph.name: SSR-005
@graph.description: cam-service shall validate that a received stream handler ID is within the configured maximum streams per connection and shall reject invalid handler IDs.
@graph.comment: Prevents out-of-bounds access and ensures monitoring resources are bounded.

@graph.name: SSR-006
@graph.description: cam-service shall verify that received stream event sequence IDs match the expected sequence for the stream and shall report a stream sequence fault on mismatch.
@graph.comment: Repo implementation checks sequence IDs and reports stream sequence faults.

@graph.name: SSR-007
@graph.description: cam-service shall verify that received event IDs follow the expected order for the stream and shall report a stream event logic fault on mismatch.
@graph.comment: CAM detects logical issues including events arriving out of order; repo implementation computes expected event ID per sequence and reports logical faults.

@graph.name: SSR-008
@graph.description: cam-service shall, for each received stream event, schedule a per-event timer based on the configured per-event timeout and report a stream event temporal fault when the timer expires before the next expected event.
@graph.comment: CAM temporal monitoring is implemented with per-event watchdog timers driven by deployment data.

@graph.name: SSR-009
@graph.description: cam-service shall reject protocol messages whose message timestamps are in the future beyond the configured clock tolerance and shall not modify monitoring state based on such messages.
@graph.comment: CAM protocol requires synchronized clocks; cam-service implements a clock tolerance check to bound timestamp anomalies.

@graph.name: SSR-010
@graph.description: cam-service shall invoke the Fault Manager driver fault-report callback upon reporting any stream fault (state, sequence, logical, temporal) or service fault and only then perform any configured post-report action.
@graph.comment: Repo fault module calls the registered fault-report callback and then performs a configured fault action (none/exit).

@graph.name: SSR-011
@graph.description: If the deployment-over-network feature is enabled, cam-service shall accept deployment messages, store the received CSD content by stream UUID with chunk-order enforcement and overwrite control, and reply with a deploy status for success or failure.
@graph.comment: CAM protocol defines a stream deploy message for development convenience and specifies status reporting for deployment outcomes.

@graph.name: SSR-020
@graph.description: libcam shall implement the Stream Message Protocol to allow critical applications to initialize streams, start/stop monitoring, and send stream event messages to cam-service over the socket-based communication channel.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation states libcam implements the message protocol and provides a high-level API for critical applications.

@graph.name: SSR-021
@graph.description: libcam shall provide a mechanism to send stream event messages with a consistent sequence identifier and event identifier such that the intended event ordering can be monitored by cam-service.
@graph.comment: cam-service verifies sequence IDs and event IDs to detect ordering/sequence faults.

@graph.name: SSR-022
@graph.description: libcam shall support a calibration/log mode where stream events are saved into a CAM Stream Event Log (CSEL) file instead of being sent to cam-service.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes libcam calibration mode producing CSEL logs for later timing analysis using cam-tool.

@graph.name: SSR-023
@graph.description: libcam shall populate protocol timestamp fields from a clock source that is synchronized with cam-service within the required tolerance for timestamp sanity checking.
@graph.comment: CAM protocol requires synchronized clocks; timestamp anomalies can cause spurious faults or rejected messages.

@graph.name: SSR-030
@graph.description: cam-tool shall convert CAM Stream Configuration (CSC) YAML files into CAM Stream Deployment (CSD) binary files suitable for consumption by cam-service.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation states cam-tool converts CSC to binary CSD for deployment to the Safety Island.

@graph.name: SSR-031
@graph.description: If used for development deployment, cam-tool shall support sending CSD deployment files to cam-service using the stream deploy message with chunking and shall handle cam-service deploy status responses.
@graph.comment: CAM message protocol defines a deploy message with chunking, and CAM documentation describes development deployments over the network.

@graph.name: SSR-032
@graph.description: cam-tool shall support reading CSEL logs to provide an initial CSC file with pre-set data extracted from the logs to support timing analysis and configuration creation.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes cam-tool analysis mode that reads CSEL and produces an initial CSC.

@graph.name: SSR-033
@graph.description: cam-tool shall validate CSC inputs during conversion, including stream UUID format, sequential event_id requirements, and non-zero required timeouts, and shall fail conversion on invalid inputs.
@graph.comment: CAM CSC specification defines constraints such as event_id starting at 0 and incrementing without gaps and non-zero start-to-event timeout; validating prevents invalid deployment data.

@graph.name: SWA-001
@graph.description: cam-service implements a socket-based communication channel for critical applications, with per-connection handling sufficient to isolate streams per connection.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation specifies a socket-based channel and that each connection spawns a new thread.

@graph.name: SWA-002
@graph.description: cam-service binds each initialized stream to deployment data selected by stream UUID and uses that configuration for monitoring.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation states cam-service matches stream UUID to deployment data; repo loads configuration at stream init.

@graph.name: SWA-003
@graph.description: cam-service maintains a stream state machine and enforces init→start and start→first-event timeouts using state timers.
@graph.comment: CAM CSC defines state_control timeouts; repo implements state timers and reports state timeout faults.

@graph.name: SWA-004
@graph.description: cam-service processes stream event messages by validating handler/state, validating sequence ID and event ID ordering, and scheduling per-event monitoring timers.
@graph.comment: Repo checks sequence and event order and schedules event timers per received event.

@graph.name: SWA-005
@graph.description: cam-service validates protocol message timestamps against its local timebase with a configurable tolerance and rejects timestamps implausibly in the future.
@graph.comment: Protocol requires synchronized clocks; repo implements a tolerance check when processing messages.

@graph.name: SWA-006
@graph.description: cam-service reports detected violations via a fault module that invokes a platform-provided fault-report callback and then performs a configured post-report action.
@graph.comment: Repo fault module calls a registered callback and then performs a configured fault action (none/exit).

@graph.name: SWA-007
@graph.description: cam-service optionally supports receiving deployment data over the socket and storing per-UUID deployment data with chunk-order enforcement and status reporting.
@graph.comment: Protocol defines deploy message chunking and statuses; repo implements deployment storage helpers.

@graph.name: SWA-008
@graph.description: libcam provides a thread-safe application-facing API that implements the Stream Message Protocol for init/start/stop/event communication with cam-service.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes libcam as thread-safe and implementing the protocol.

@graph.name: SWA-009
@graph.description: libcam supports a mode where stream events are written to a CSEL log file instead of being sent to cam-service.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes CSEL log mode used for timing analysis via cam-tool.

@graph.name: SWA-010
@graph.description: cam-tool implements conversion from CSC YAML to CSD binary with input validation according to the CSC specification.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation defines CSC and CSD file specifications and cam-tool conversion.

@graph.name: SWA-011
@graph.description: cam-tool supports sending CSD deployment files to cam-service over the protocol deploy message using chunking and response status handling.
@graph.comment: Protocol deploy message defines chunking and status codes; CAM docs describe this as a development convenience.

@graph.name: SWA-012
@graph.description: cam-tool supports analyzing CSEL logs to generate an initial CSC file with extracted timing data.
@graph.comment: CAM documentation describes cam-tool CSEL analysis producing an initial CSC.

@graph.description: Missing/late event triggers temporal fault and fault reporting.

@graph.name: TC-002
@graph.description: Out-of-order event triggers logical fault and fault reporting.

@graph.name: TC-003
@graph.description: Sequence mismatch triggers sequence fault and fault reporting.

@graph.name: TC-004
@graph.description: Start-to-first-event timeout triggers state timeout fault and reporting.

@graph.name: TC-005
@graph.description: Event before start triggers stream state fault and reporting.

@graph.name: TC-006
@graph.description: CSC validation and CSC→CSD conversion support correct cam-service configuration loading by UUID.

@graph.name: TC-007
@graph.description: Deploy messages are chunked and status-handled correctly in development deployment.

@graph.name: TC-008
@graph.description: Future timestamps beyond tolerance are rejected without unsafe state changes.

@graph.name: TC-009
@graph.description: libcam CSEL generation and cam-tool analysis produce an initial CSC.

@graph.name: TC-010
@graph.description: libcam executes a compliant init/start/event/stop protocol sequence.

@graph.name: TC-011
@graph.description: Malformed messages and out-of-range handler IDs are rejected safely.
